3 Examples
sections.text: Code for the examples and plots can be found at: https://github.com/bemigini/cosine-sim-not-informative . 3.1 Example using Unrestricted Unembeddings We assume three models as in Fig. 1 , where all three models have embeddings as in Fig. 1 a) , and b) , c) , d) are the three different sets of unembeddings. The unembeddings of the first model corresponding to the five labels are in order 0 to 4: 𝐥 0 = ( 1 0.5 ) , 𝐥 1 = ( 0.5 1 ) , 𝐥 2 = ( − 1 0.4 ) , 𝐥 3 = ( − 0.8 − 0.8 ) , 𝐥 4 = ( 0.9 − 1.2 ) . \displaystyle\mathbf{l}_{0}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\ 0.5\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{1}=\begin{pmatrix}0.5\\ 1\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{2}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\ 0.4\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{3}=\begin{pmatrix}-0.8\\ -0.8\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{4}=\begin{pmatrix}0.9\\ -1.2\end{pmatrix}\;. (13) We see that the cosine similarity between unembeddings corresponding to labels 0 0 and 1 1 is: cos ⁡ ( 𝐥 0 , 𝐥 1 ) = 1 1.25 = 0.8 . \displaystyle\cos(\mathbf{l}_{0},\mathbf{l}_{1})=\frac{1}{1.25}=0.8\;. (14) The unembeddings for the second model ( Fig. 1 c) ) are constructed by taking 𝐯 \mathbf{v} as in Lemma 2.2 , so we take 𝐯 = − 𝐥 0 − 1 2 ​ ( 𝐥 1 − 𝐥 0 ) = − ( 1 0.5 ) − 1 2 ​ ( ( 0.5 1 ) − ( 1 0.5 ) ) = ( − 0.75 − 0.75 ) . \displaystyle\mathbf{v}=-\mathbf{l}_{0}-\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{l}_{1}-\mathbf{l}_{0})=-\begin{pmatrix}1\\ 0.5\end{pmatrix}-\frac{1}{2}\left(\begin{pmatrix}0.5\\ 1\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}1\\ 0.5\end{pmatrix}\right)=\begin{pmatrix}-0.75\\ -0.75\end{pmatrix}\;. (15) The unembeddings of the second model are then 𝐥 i + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{i}+\mathbf{v} and the cosine similarity between 𝐥 0 + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{0}+\mathbf{v} and 𝐥 1 + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{1}+\mathbf{v} is: cos ⁡ ( 𝐥 0 + 𝐯 , 𝐥 1 + 𝐯 ) = − 1 . \displaystyle\cos(\mathbf{l}_{0}+\mathbf{v},\mathbf{l}_{1}+\mathbf{v})=-1\;. (16) The unembeddings for the third model ( Fig. 1 d) ) are constructed by taking 𝐯 \mathbf{v} as in Lemma 2.3 . That is, 𝐯 = − 𝐥 0 + 1 2 ​ ( 𝐥 1 − 𝐥 0 ) , \displaystyle\mathbf{v}=-\mathbf{l}_{0}+\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{l}_{1}-\mathbf{l}_{0})\;, (17) the unembeddings are 𝐥 i + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{i}+\mathbf{v} and the cosine similarity between 𝐥 0 + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{0}+\mathbf{v} and 𝐥 1 + 𝐯 \mathbf{l}_{1}+\mathbf{v} is: cos ⁡ ( 𝐥 0 + 𝐯 , 𝐥 1 + 𝐯 ) = 1 . \displaystyle\cos(\mathbf{l}_{0}+\mathbf{v},\mathbf{l}_{1}+\mathbf{v})=1\;. (18) 3.2 Example using Centered Unembeddings Figure 2: Examples of models with centered unembeddings. In both cases, we see that a high (or low) cosine similarity between unembeddings does not guarantee that the corresponding labels will have high (or low) probability for possible inputs. Left: These unembeddings are centered. Right: These unembeddings are centered and have length 1 1 . We here present an example of a model with centered unembeddings illustrated in Fig. 2 left. For the five labels the unembeddings are: 𝐥 0 = ( 1.4 − 1 ) , 𝐥 1 = ( 1.4 1 ) , 𝐥 2 = ( − 0.9 0.3 ) , 𝐥 3 = ( − 1 0 ) , 𝐥 4 = ( − 0.9 − 0.3 ) . \displaystyle\mathbf{l}_{0}=\begin{pmatrix}1.4\\ -1\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{1}=\begin{pmatrix}1.4\\ 1\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{2}=\begin{pmatrix}-0.9\\ 0.3\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{3}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\ 0\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{4}=\begin{pmatrix}-0.9\\ -0.3\end{pmatrix}\;. (19) These unembeddings are centered since the sum is the zero vector. The cosine similarity between 𝐥 0 \mathbf{l}_{0} and 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} is approximately 0.3 0.3 and between 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} and 𝐥 2 \mathbf{l}_{2} it is approximately − 0.6 -0.6 , however for both these pairs of labels it is possible to place embeddings which will result in equal probability for both labels. On the other hand, the cosine similarity between 𝐥 2 \mathbf{l}_{2} and 𝐥 4 \mathbf{l}_{4} is 0.8 0.8 , but it is not possible for these labels to be tied for the highest probability, since if we place an embeddings between them, the dot-product with 𝐥 3 \mathbf{l}_{3} would be higher. This example also shows us that neighbourhoods using cosine similarity do also not correspond to probabilities: The two nearest neighbours of 𝐥 2 \mathbf{l}_{2} in terms of cosine similarity are 𝐥 3 \mathbf{l}_{3} and 𝐥 4 \mathbf{l}_{4} , but the the two labels with which 𝐥 2 \mathbf{l}_{2} can have tied for highest probabilities are 𝐥 3 \mathbf{l}_{3} and 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} . 3.3 Example using Centered Unembeddings of Length 1 We here present an example of a model with centered unembeddings which all have length 1 1 illustrated in Fig. 2 right. For the five labels the unembeddings are: 𝐥 0 = ( 0.95 1 − 0.95 2 ) , 𝐥 1 = ( − 0.95 1 − 0.95 2 ) , 𝐥 2 = ( − 1 0 ) , \displaystyle\mathbf{l}_{0}=\begin{pmatrix}0.95\\ \sqrt{1-0.95^{2}}\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{1}=\begin{pmatrix}-0.95\\ \sqrt{1-0.95^{2}}\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{2}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\ 0\end{pmatrix}\;, (20) 𝐥 3 = ( − 0.95 1 − 0.95 2 ) , 𝐥 4 = ( 0.95 1 − 0.95 2 ) , 𝐥 5 = ( 1 0 ) . \displaystyle\mathbf{l}_{3}=\begin{pmatrix}-0.95\\ \sqrt{1-0.95^{2}}\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{4}=\begin{pmatrix}0.95\\ \sqrt{1-0.95^{2}}\end{pmatrix}\;,\;\mathbf{l}_{5}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\ 0\end{pmatrix}\;. (21) We see that these sum to the zero vector and each of them has norm 1 1 . We see that the cosine similarity between 𝐥 0 \mathbf{l}_{0} and 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} is approximately − 0.8 -0.8 , while between 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} and 𝐥 3 \mathbf{l}_{3} it is approximately 0.8 0.8 . At the same time, 𝐥 0 \mathbf{l}_{0} and 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} can be tied for highest probability, while 𝐥 3 \mathbf{l}_{3} and 𝐥 1 \mathbf{l}_{1} cannot.

sections.heading: 4 Discussion and Further Questions
sections.text: This result means that when working with softmax classifiers, we should not use cosine similarity between the unembeddings to say something about the assigned probabilities of the models. On the other hand, this result says nothing about whether cosine similarity is a meaningful measure to use between embeddings, as for example the probabilities of a softmax classifier are not invariant to vector translations of the input representations. In Nielsen et al. (2025) they saw that when comparing token representations with each other it often resulted in nuisance hubness and therefore advocate for hubness reduction techniques. However, this work shows that the similarity measures themselves do not carry information about the probabilities, and this will probably not be fixed by doing hubness reduction. As a last clarification, how unembeddings are placed in relation to each other is important for model probabilities in the sense that two unembeddings sharing a decision boundary can have very similar dot products for the same input and therefore their labels can be likely at the same time. What this paper shows is that cosine similarity cannot reliably be used to tell whether two umebeddings will share a decision boundary or not and thus should not be used for that purpose.
